blocks.text: Re: Reputation audit
Dear Robert:

We were pleased to learn that {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} (the "Company") would like to proceed, and this letter sets out the terms on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC ("Ashcombe," "we" or "us") will conduct a reputation audit on its behalf. We have tried to describe the work plainly, so that you and your colleagues know what to expect of us and what we will ask of you in return.
Purpose and Scope

The purpose of the audit is to give the Company's leadership an accurate and independent picture of how the Company is regarded today by investors and analysts, by the financial and trade press, and in online discussion. We will set that outside view against the way the Company presents itself, and identify where the two diverge and, as far as the evidence allows, why.

The scope is limited to assessment and recommendation. Unless we agree otherwise in writing, it does not include drafting or issuing announcements, media relations on the Company's behalf, or support in the event of a crisis, although we would be glad to discuss any of these separately should the need arise.
Our Approach

We will begin with a review of the Company's public record, including its announcements, investor materials and website, together with the coverage they have attracted. Alongside that review, we will hold confidential conversations with members of your leadership team and, with your approval of each name in advance, with a selection of investors, analysts and reporters who follow the Company.

Where it is useful, we will also look at how a small number of comparable companies are covered, so that the Company's position can be read in context rather than in isolation. We will agree the choice of those companies with you before we begin that comparison.

We will share our emerging observations with you informally before they are committed to writing, so that nothing in the final product comes as a surprise. The audit will conclude with a written report of findings and recommendations, which we will present to you and to any colleagues you wish to include.
Who Will Do the Work

I will lead the engagement personally and will remain responsible for the quality of its conclusions. Michelle Rose, a Communications Associate, will manage the work from day to day and conduct our conversations with the press, and Kimberly Le, a Communications Analyst, will lead our review of news and online coverage.

We understand that you will act as the Company's principal contact for the engagement. Unless you direct otherwise, we will route our requests for documents, introductions and scheduling through you. Should the needs of the engagement call for other members of the firm, we will tell you before involving them.
What We Will Ask of the Company

The value of an audit of this kind depends in large part on candor and access. We will ask the Company to provide the materials we reasonably request, to make the members of its leadership team available for interviews, and to tell us promptly of any development that may bear on how the Company is perceived while the work is under way.
Commencement and Fee

We will begin work on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}. For the audit as described in this letter, the Company will pay Ashcombe a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}}, which covers the professional time of the full team through delivery and presentation of the final report.
The fee will not change unless the scope does. If you ask us to extend the work, we will agree any additional fee with you in writing before we begin it.
Billing and Payment

We will invoice the fixed fee in monthly installments over the course of the engagement, and each invoice is payable upon receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as travel undertaken at your request, will be billed at cost and only with your prior approval.
Duration and Termination

The engagement will continue until we have delivered and presented our final report, unless it is ended sooner. Either party may terminate it at any time by written notice to the other, in which case the Company will pay for work performed and approved expenses incurred up to the effective date of termination.
Confidential Information

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company provides to us, and all that we learn in the course of our interviews, and we will use it only for the purposes of this engagement. Those we interview will be told that their views will be shared with the Company in summary form and without attribution, and our report will honor that undertaking.

These obligations do not extend to information that is or becomes public through no fault of ours, or that we are required by law to disclose. They will survive the conclusion or termination of the engagement, and at your request we will return or destroy the Company's materials once the work is complete, subject to our ordinary record-keeping obligations.
Limits of Liability

Our findings will reflect our professional judgment, based on the information available to us and the views of those we interview, and we cannot guarantee any particular response from investors, analysts or the press. Except in the case of our gross negligence or willful misconduct, our aggregate liability arising from this engagement will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses.
Our role is advisory. Decisions about the Company's communications, and responsibility for any statement the Company makes publicly, remain with the Company.
Governing Law

This letter will be governed by the laws of the state in which Ashcombe maintains its principal office, without regard to its conflict-of-law principles. It constitutes the entire agreement between us with respect to the audit and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties.

We are looking forward to working with you. If these terms reflect your understanding, please sign below and return a copy to me, and Michelle Rose will contact you the same day to arrange the first of the leadership interviews.
Signed for Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC and, in acceptance of these terms, for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}:
Kickoff Memo: Reputation Audit

To: Julie Hill, Kimberly Le
From: Michelle Rose
Re: {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}, opening plan

The reputation audit for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} opened on {{fact:f:E-2024-001.start}}. Our job is to find out how investors, analysts, reporters and online audiences see the company now, where that picture departs from the company's own account of itself, and what is causing the gap. The end product is a written findings report with recommendations, presented to the client at the close.

Robert Smith, VP Finance, is our sponsor and our route to everyone on the client side. His main interest is the investor and analyst view. The press and online work matters because it feeds that view. Julie Hill leads the engagement and signs off on every conclusion. I run the work day to day.
How the work divides

Public record. I am collecting the company's announcements, investor materials and website copy into one file of what the company says about itself. Each item gets tagged by theme so we can set it against the coverage.

Coverage and online discussion. Kimberly Le owns the coverage baseline: news, trade press and social channels over the review period, coded for tone and topic. She will flag anything that is still moving. We need a first cut of this before any external interview takes place. She will also pull coverage for a short list of comparable companies, so the client's coverage can be read in context.

Leadership interviews. Robert has agreed to arrange time with the senior team. I will draft the interview guide and send it to Julie Hill for review before it goes to him. Every interview is confidential and reported without attribution.

External interviews. Robert approves each investor, analyst and reporter before we make contact. I will take the reporter conversations, on background, starting with people we already know. Julie will take the investor and analyst calls herself.
Synthesis. Findings come together once the interviews close. We walk Robert through early observations before anything is written up. No finding goes to the client without Julie's sign-off.

Timing. The interviews are the long pole. Leadership calendars are not ours to control, so the guide has to be ready before Robert starts asking for time. Julie wants an interim readout for Robert around the midpoint, built on whatever the interviews have shown by then.
House rules for this one

Client documents go in the engagement folder, not in personal drives or inboxes. Interview notes stay internal. Status updates go to Robert by email with the three of us copied, so the thread is the record.

Outside interviews carry some risk of the audit becoming a story. Nobody we approach is told more than that we are gathering views on the company's behalf. If a reporter calls back asking for comment on anything, it comes to Julie before anyone answers.
What happens first

Kimberly, please start the coverage pull now. A rough baseline by the end of next week is enough to shape the interview guide. Julie, you will have the guide and a draft list of external names from me early next week.
Before any of that, I will send Robert our document request today so his team can start gathering.
Hello Robert,
Here is a short update on the reputation audit, and one request.

We have finished our first pass through the public record for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}: its announcements, investor materials and website, set against the news and online coverage Kimberly Le has gathered over the same period. That coverage is now coded by tone and topic. It gives us a working baseline to test in the interviews. A few themes already recur; we will bring them to you once the interviews have confirmed or challenged them.

The interviews come next. We have a draft guide for the leadership conversations and a draft list of external names, made up of investors, analysts and reporters who follow the company. No one outside the company has been contacted, and no one will be until you approve the name. Each leadership conversation should take under an hour and can be held by video if that suits your team better.

The request is your review of that list, which I will send separately this afternoon. Please mark any names to add or drop, and note anyone you would prefer to contact first yourself. Once we have it back, we will start scheduling the leadership interviews.
Thanks,
Robert,

One addition to Michelle's note as you review the list. If an investor or analyst has raised a concern about {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} with you directly, even informally, we would ask you to flag the name; those conversations tend to tell us the most, and we will approach them with appropriate care.

We would also suggest that the investor and analyst calls wait until the leadership interviews are complete, so that we go into them with a fair sense of how your own team sees things. Could we find a short call this week to walk through the list together?

Thanks,
JH
Hello Robert,
Thank you for walking through the list with us. The changes you asked for are made, and the version we hold now matches what you approved.

We will keep to the order Julie suggested. The leadership interviews go first, and the invitations will go out as soon as you confirm the final names. The investor and analyst calls follow once that round is finished.

On the press side, I have started background conversations with the reporters you cleared, beginning with those who follow {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} most closely. Nothing you have shared with us comes up in those calls.
Please send the final leadership names when you have them, and I will issue the invitations the same day.
Thanks,
Robert,

A brief word on the reporter conversations Michelle mentioned, since your colleagues may ask about them. They are held on background only; we neither speak for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} nor characterize its plans, and what we hear will reach you as themes in summary form rather than as notes of individual calls.

If there is any outlet you would prefer we not approach, a note to Michelle is enough, and we will set it aside. I will send you a short summary of the early themes once the leadership round is complete.

Thanks,
JH
